minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  Public Improvement Corporation,
  and Library Board of Trustees*

  April 19, 2010

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, the Public Improvement Corporation, and the Library Board
of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Kelley at 5:00
p.m., on April 19, 2010, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on April 14, 2010, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Ledesma (arrived at 5:15 p.m.)
  Council Member Schlicht (arrived at 5:11 p.m.)
  Mayor Pro Tem Leckness
  Mayor Kelley

Absent:  Council Member Ury (present from 5:00 to 5:45 only)

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Irwin B. Bornstein, Assistant City Manager/Director of Admin. Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Ury

INVOCATION: Mayor Pro Tem Leckness

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Labor Negotiations - The Council Will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6. The Parties to the Negotiations Are the
  City and City's Unrepresented Employees. The City’s Negotiator is Dennis Wilberg.

City Council Minutes  1  April 19, 2010
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:09 p.m., Mayor Kelley recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:02 p.m. with four City Council Members present. Council Member Ury
had a family commitment and departed the meeting during Closed Session at 5:45 p.m.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the City Council received information but there was no
reportable action from Closed Session.

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Presentation by Roseann Andrus of Child Care Connections to the City of Mission
  Viejo for an Excellence in Child Care Planning Award

  Mayor Kelley received the award from Roseann Andrus of Child Care Connections.

P2.  Proclaim April 2010 as Organ Donation Awareness Month

  Mayor Kelley presented the proclamation to Lorraine and Victor Kobett.

P3.  Arts Alive Presentation

  Director of Library Services Valerie Maginnis and Director of Public Services Keith
  Rattay presented the Arts Alive schedule of events.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Joyce Saltzgiver, Member of the Casta del Sol Homeowners Association Board of Directors,
M.V.: expressed objection to the proposed median island cut-through on Casta del Sol Drive for
egress to the Tennis Center.

Dan Avery, M.V.: regarding opposition to the dog park, he stated that complaints are not
relevant to developing this city and are only relevant to freezing it in time.

Neil Lonsinger, M.V.: suggested that residents concerned about city streets should work with
staff via the reporting process that has been set in place.

Jeff Willis, M.V.: stated that Measure D will damage the City of Mission Viejo, will make the
city unable to respond to changing conditions and will freeze land use forever. He feels that the
measure is poorly written and will strangle business growth.

Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: on behalf of the Chamber of Commerce, she expressed concern about

City Council Minutes  2  April 19, 2010
 Measure D and stated that it disproportionately targets business owners, churches, and hospitals.
The Chamber opposes the measure and will work to defeat it.

Dennis O’Connor, M.V.: speaking as a member of the Orange County Association of Realtors
and the South Orange County Regional Chambers of Commerce, he stated that he is very much
opposed to Measure D.

Cameron Mirsaidi, M.V.: expressed concern with plans for a third group home on Avenida
Calidad and stated that he is worried about the safety of children who live in the vicinity.

Nancy Cho, M.V.: announced that the Melinda House is hosting an exhibit on the history of
aviation in Orange County and, on behalf of the Mission Viejo Heritage Committee, she thanked
the City Council for their support. She also announced that Mission Viejo History Books and
playing cards will be sold at Arts Alive and the Saddleback College Veterans Memorial
dedication will be held on April 29, 2010 at 4:00 p.m.

Joan Snow, M.V.: stated that she represents at least 20 other neighbors from Avenida Calidad
who are concerned with a potential third residential care facility on that street. The contractor
told neighbors that he was going to live in the house but it is now being developed as a group
home and she asked the Council for input.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 8 and 10 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to approve
the Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, and Schlicht
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Ury

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said
  titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title
  and further reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the Regular City Council Meeting of April 5, 2010, as
  presented.

City Council Minutes  3  April 19, 2010
 3.  Check Register dated March 26, 2010, in the amount of $2,865,728.13

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register dated April 2, 2010, in the amount of $553,385.32

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  City Treasurer's Monthly Report for February 2010

  Received and filed.

6.  Community Development Agency Treasurer's Monthly Report for February 2010

  Received and filed.

7.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer's Monthly Report for February 2010

  Received and filed.

9.  2010 Residential Resurfacing (CIP 838)

  (1) Approved the bid specifications and authorized staff to advertise for construction bids
  for the subject project and (2) adopted Resolution 10-16 Amending The Fiscal Year
  2009-2010 Budget To Increase Funding For CIP 838.

11.  Oso/Marguerite Intersection Improvements (CIP 844)

  Approved payment in the amount of $181,717.00 to San Diego Gas & Electric Company
  (Sempra Energy) for the relocation of street lights and certain electrical facilities.

12.  Investment Advisory Commission Vacancy

  (1) Declared a vacancy on the Investment Advisory Commission as a result of
  Commissioner Standish's resignation; and (2) directed the City Clerk to post the notice of
  unscheduled vacancy.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

13.  Appeal of Planned Development Permit PDP2009-221 Filed by Council Member
  Cathy Schlicht of the Planning and Transportation Commission’s February 8, 2010
  Approval of a City Initiated Petition Submitted by the City of Mission Viejo
  Recreation and Community Services Department for the Marguerite Tennis,

City Council Minutes  4  April 19, 2010
   Aquatics, and Recreation Center Complex Renovation and Expansion Project at
  23840 Marguerite Parkway, in the R (Recreation) and RPD 6.5 (Residential
  Planned Development) Zones.

  Director of Community Development Chuck Wilson presented the staff report.

  Larry Ryan, RJM Design Group: provided an overview of the scope of the project and the
  potential phasing.

  Council Member Schlicht stated this is a very important issue and she would prefer to
  have Council Member Ury present when this matter is considered.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to
  continue the public hearing to the meeting of May 3, 2010.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, and Schlicht
  NOES:  Ledesma
  ABSENT: Ury

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, seconded by Council Member Schlicht, to
  open the public hearing to allow those who cannot attend the next meeting to speak
  tonight.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: Ury

  At the hour of 7:26 p.m., Mayor Kelley opened the public hearing to hear the testimony
  of residents who cannot attend the next meeting.

  The following expressed concern with the appeal and spoke in support of the Tennis
  Center renovation project: Tom Teichmann, M.V.; Wendy Bucknum, M.V.; and
  Shripathi Kamath, M.V.

  The following presented photographs depicting areas of the tennis courts that need repair:
  Kime Goodrum, M.V.

  At the hour of 7:34 p.m., Mayor Kelley continued the public hearing to May 3, 2010.

City Council Minutes  5  April 19, 2010
 OLD BUSINESS

14.  Mission Viejo Dog Park

  Director of Recreation and Community Services Kelly Doyle presented the staff report.

  The following spoke in support of a Mission Viejo dog park at the Felipe/Arroyo Site:
  Nermine Marcos, M.V.; Neil Lonsinger, M.V.; Joey Sellers, M.V.; Susan Sellers, M.V.;
  and Sharon Cody, M.V.

  The following spoke in opposition to the proposed dog park location due to the potential
  cost: Paula Berg, M.V. and Anita Robertson, M.V.

  Motion made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Mayor Kelley, to (1) approve
  the Felipe-Arroyo (Gilleran Park) site for a possible dog park; and (2) direct staff to issue
  a Request for Proposal for architectural and construction management services for
  contract bid documents for the construction of the dog park.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Leckness, Ledesma, and Kelley
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT: Ury

NEW BUSINESS

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

8.  Marguerite Aquatics and Tennis Center Renovation (CIPs #314 and 501)

  Director of Recreation and Community Services Kelly Doyle presented the staff report.

  Council Member Schlicht asked how the project went from $38,000 to $45,000.

  Cheryl Hodge, President, Hodge & Associates: stated that there were two contract
  amendments to accommodate additional technical work associated with the parking and
  traffic studies. The third contract amendment is for the consultants’ appearance at
  tonight's public hearing for agenda item #13.

  Motion made by Mayor Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to approve
  Amendment #3 to the contract with Hodge & Associates for additional environmental
  consulting services in the amount of $1,395.

City Council Minutes  6  April 19, 2010
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Leckness, Ledesma, and Kelley
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT: Ury

10.  2010 Orange County International Triathlon in Mission Viejo

  Mayor Kelley stated that she removed this item from the Consent Calendar to provide
  background and give exposure to the event.

  Bill Leach: discussed the Triathlon's history, stated that there is very little impact to
  residents and he looks forward to this year’s event. He also thanked the City Council for
  their support.

  Motion made by Mayor Kelley, seconded by Council Member Schlicht, to approve the
  request submitted by Pelican Coast Events, LLC, to hold the 2010 Orange County
  International Triathlon in Mission Viejo on Sunday, October 10, 2010.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: Ury

RECESS

At the hour of 8:54 p.m., Mayor Kelley declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 9:06
p.m. with four City Council Members present (Council Member Ury was absent).

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

15.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Mayor Kelley presented the report.

16.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Kelley announced that she attended the last TCA meeting on Council Member
  Ury's behalf and she presented the report.

17.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Kelley presented the report.

City Council Minutes  7  April 19, 2010
 STAFF REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS

18.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
  presented in the staff report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the
  public record.

  Council Member Schlicht protested the City Manager’s disapproval of her AB 1234
  report. She stated that she was in court to represent herself as a City Council Member
  supporting the residents of the City of Mission Viejo in regard to Measure D and she
  would like to be reimbursed for her mileage and parking fees.

  City Manager Wilberg said that he believes that the Judge ruled that Council Member
  Schlicht was in court as a private resident/voter. The city’s policy doesn’t allow him to
  approve reimbursement for anyone other than Council Members. He noted that the
  Council has the authority to approve the request and this can be considered at the next
  City Council meeting if the City Council desires.

  By consensus, the City Council directed staff to place this item on the next agenda.

Council Member Ledesma

Council Member Schlicht

19.  Transparency in Government

  Council Member Schlicht stated that she would like to postpone this item due to personal
  reasons.

Ms. Schlicht re-addressed the Hodge & Associates payment (agenda item #8) and stated that the
contract required attendance at two public hearings yet Mrs. Hodge admitted that she only
attended one meeting. Council Member Schlicht stated that to her, this is double-dipping
because there was never an amendment to change the meeting attendance requirements. Council
Member Schlicht reported on her attendance at the April 15 TEA Party and noted that the City
didn't acknowledge the event in any of its literature. She felt that it was a great event and she
was pleased to see over 600 attendees. She expressed concern about the lack of reporting in the
Orange County Register and she read a quote, in part stating that "only a free and unrestrained
press can effectively expose deception in government."

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness wished Polish-American resident Ziggy Wilczynski a happy 89th

City Council Minutes  8  April 19, 2010
 birthday. He also noted that the country of Poland is experiencing a very difficult time with the
loss of their President, Lech Kaczynski, his wife and several military leaders. Mayor Pro Tem
Leckness announced that former LAPD Chief Darryl Gates was hospitalized in Mission Viejo
before he passed away on April 16, 2010, and he thanked Mayor Kelley and staff member
Jennifer Myers for putting together a very nice commendation for the former police chief. Mr.
Gates had expressed his appreciation for the gesture and for the excellent care he received at
Mission Hospital.

Mayor Kelley

Council Member Schlicht departed the meeting at 9:22 p.m. and did not return.

Mayor Kelley announced that Arts Alive will be a spectacular two day event on April 24 and 25,
2010, and she highlighted the activities that will take place. She noted that Rachel’s Challenge
and Fun With Chalk are still looking for volunteers, and those interested can contact her or
Elaine Lieberman for more information. Mayor Kelley expressed pride in the Mission Viejo
High School (MVHS) Color Guard team that won a bronze medal at the Winter Guard
International World Championships in Dayton, Ohio. The sixteen-member team will compete
again on Sunday, April 25, in Rancho Cucamonga and she extended the city’s congratulations to
the coaches and the team. Mayor Kelley reminded residents that the Saddleback College
Veterans Memorial Dedication will be held on April 29, 2010, at 4:00 p.m. and she encouraged
residents to attend. She also announced that six Carl Hankey Elementary School students are
moving on to an international competition after winning 1st place at the state Destination
Imagination competition on April 10 in San Jose. The girls are Jessica Fleck, Shelby Capozzoli,
Alli Maynard, Jessie McGee, Valerie Sierakowski, and Kamela Kadri. Destination Imagination,
which involves approximately 100,000 students in the United States, is an educational program
where students work in teams to solve problems creatively without the help of their parents.
Mayor Kelley further congratulated Capistrano Valley High School for winning an essay contest
that netted the school $200,000 in cutting-edge Samsung products. She also outlined the
upcoming Writers Present series events with authors Meg Cabot and Henry Winkler and
announced that the City of Mission Viejo was named Employer of the Year by the California
Disabilities Services Association and she expressed gratitude for the recognition. Finally, Mayor
Kelley encouraged those who have questions about a potential CUSD teachers’ strike to visit the
District’s web site at www.capousd.org and she stated that she hopes for the best as this impacts
our children.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:31 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Kelley adjourned the meeting in memory of Brad Clark to Monday, May 3, 2010, at 5:00 p.m.

__________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of May 3, 2010

City Council Minutes  9  April 19, 2010
